items.headline: FMRB executive order Monday open: CISA Director joins witness slate; ACLU + CDT amicus filing extends coalition
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday the Sunday cycle added long-read State Farm reasoned-decision-record arguments from Lawfare and customary-international-practice arguments from Just Security alongside two new May 15 witnesses (NSA Cybersecurity Directorate director plus a Microsoft Threat Intelligence Center representative) bringing the briefing toward an operational view of Mythos-class enterprise exposure. Today the witness slate firms to five with CISA Director joining Locascio + ODNI cyber lead + NSA Cyber + MSTIC, focusing the operational view on federal-civilian-executive-branch agentic-AI exposure; ACLU + Center for Democracy and Technology file a joint Monday amicus letter joining the existing coalition (AI Policy Institute / R Street / Public Knowledge / Lawyers for Civil Justice / Knight First Amendment Institute / EFF) pressing the State Farm reasoned-decision record argument plus 60-day DPA Section 708 public-comment window. OSTP confirms no signing window before May 22, putting the May 21 federal-civilian n8n CVE remediation deadline before the earliest EO signing date.

items.headline: Indo-Pacific reciprocity perimeter crosses ten named jurisdictions with Indonesia and Vietnam
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday the Sunday cycle lifted the perimeter to eight named candidates (Singapore, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand formally; Canada, Australia, India, Taiwan as observers) plus the UK + EU originating pair, with India MeitY + CERT-In on a 180-day window targeting Q4 2026 mirror-signature and Taiwan NICS confirming Track II observer entry. Today Indonesia's BSSN + Kominfo enter as formal observers with a 150-day consultation window targeting Q4 2026 mirror-signature, and Vietnam MIC confirms observer entry under Track II shoulder-to-shoulder arrangements parallel to Taiwan's Sunday announcement, lifting the cohort to ten named candidates. Mistral + Anthropic + OpenAI + Google DeepMind reaffirm cohort participation; the operational threshold remains Mythos plus GPT-5.5. The US recognition gap is now a full Monday wider than the Friday baseline.

items.headline: Cerebras CBRS Monday gap-up to $189.40 validates Sunday buyside targets; second trading week opens with 3.8x call-skew
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's Sunday note season pre-positioned the trade: Morgan Stanley raised CBRS to $192 from $185, Goldman held $185 with a $220 upside scenario tied to Saudi Aramco Digital MoU, Bernstein kept Market-Perform at $172 with single-counterparty risk in its own subheading, Jefferies initiated Buy at $178, and CBRS options heading into Monday sat at approximately 51,200 calls vs 14,700 puts (3.5x call-skew). Today the second-week open prints $189.40 — up 9.5 percent from Friday's $172.85 close — validating the Morgan Stanley/Jefferies/Goldman target raises without testing the Bernstein floor; Bernstein issues a Monday-morning maintenance note moving single-counterparty-concentration risk to a more prominent placement but holds the rating. CBRS options widen to a 3.8x call-skew at 11:00 EDT (approximately 54,800 calls vs 14,600 puts). The Saudi Aramco Digital MoU close remains the operative Q3 catalyst; CBRS continues to anchor the Tenstorrent + SambaNova next-wave pricing reference set.

items.headline: Tenstorrent files confidential S-1 pre-submission cover note; SEC filing window opens Monday
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Tenstorrent's Sunday investor-relations note added Citi as joint lead bookrunner alongside J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley plus Mizuho Securities and SMBC Nikko as Asia-Pacific co-managers reflecting Hyundai + Samsung Foundry co-anchor positions; SambaNova added Wells Fargo Securities to its syndicate at the $7-9B fully-diluted range; a Reuters Asia wire flagged early discussion of a Saudi PIF contingent secondary for Groq. Today Tenstorrent files the confidential S-1 pre-submission cover note with the SEC, opening the filing window per the JOBS Act EGC framework; the submission cover discloses the J.P. Morgan + Morgan Stanley + Citi bookrunner triad plus Mizuho + SMBC Nikko Asia-Pacific co-managers, with Bain Capital Ventures + Fidelity + Vy Capital + Atomico + Founders Fund participating at the $3.4B bridge-round valuation. Jim Keller's Monday IR note ratifies the early-August public-filing window pending standard SEC 30-60 day review. SambaNova's Monday market-conditions update confirms Wells Fargo as joint lead with late-June confidential-submission target unchanged. Groq remains 30-60 days behind pending Saudi closure.

items.headline: Mag-7 Monday primer: Bernstein lifts Alphabet AI-Services-footnote probability to 65 percent (from 55 percent Friday)
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's 247 Wall St Sunday valuation circular named May 21 Alphabet analyst day the operative pricing event for the Mag-7 AI Services 10-Q footnote breakout probability, with VentureBeat noting Wells Fargo expected Alphabet to ship a Q2 AI Services footnote shape mirroring Microsoft's previously-guided fiscal Q1 2027 breakout. Today Bernstein + Wells Fargo Securities + Evercore ISI each publish Monday-morning preview circulars naming May 21 the operative pricing event; Bernstein raises the Alphabet Q2 AI Services footnote probability to 65 percent (from 55 percent in Friday's note). VentureBeat aggregates the cohort take with Wells Fargo now expecting Meta + AWS to follow within one quarter once Alphabet confirms the shape. The May 8 SEC Corp Fin sample comment letter remains the policy anchor; the Cerebras CBRS post-IPO Monday open now provides the operative valuation comparable for the AI-accelerator-revenue multiple band.

items.headline: Ni8mare day-eleven: Monday-open commodity-tier exploit-kit spike materializes at 6.4x baseline
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Shadowserver's day-ten scan dropped exposed pre-1.121.0 n8n instances to approximately 5,700 (-16.2 percent vs Saturday) with 38 percent unpatched on the residual long tail; Aikido's Sunday telemetry noted exploitation attempts held at approximately 2.9x baseline awaiting Monday-open commodity-tier activity. Today's day-eleven scan continues the descent to approximately 4,920 (-13.7 percent from Sunday) with the US cohort at 1,650 and India at 875; unpatched share falls to 33 percent. Censys telemetry confirms the long-awaited Monday-open spike — exploitation attempts jump to approximately 6.4x baseline at 09:00 UTC, with Microsoft Defender for Cloud + CrowdStrike Falcon + SentinelOne Singularity publishing a joint Monday telemetry note attributing the spike to Cobalt Strike + Sliver + Mythic C2 frameworks staged through the Ni8mare credential-stuffing entrypoint. The May 21 federal-civilian remediation deadline holds.

items.headline: MCP-server attack-surface: unprotected-vs-protected gap stretches to 30x; Cisco-Astrix tenancy reaches 1,180
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Sysdig's Sunday addendum showed unprotected-estate median time-to-first-credential-extraction collapsing from 19 to 14 minutes while Defender-protected held at 4.3 hours (23 percent gap widening in one cycle); Wiz Research placed exposed MCP servers at approximately 9,800 with Defender quarantine at 28 percent and Cisco-Astrix identity-gateway tenancy at 920 (+24 percent vs Saturday). Today Sysdig's Monday note reports the unprotected-estate median collapses further from 14 to 8 minutes (-43 percent in 24 hours) while Defender-protected holds at approximately 4.0 hours — the gap now stretches 30x. Wiz reports Defender-for-Cloud quarantine on net-new MCP servers reaches 32 percent (vs 28 percent Sunday); Cisco-Astrix identity-gateway tenancy crosses 1,180 (vs 920 Sunday, +28 percent), with Akamai SkyAtlas MCP-firewall reaching 510 tenants in parallel. Cross-vendor control-plane visibility holds above 68 percent (from 65 percent Sunday).

items.headline: LangChain CVE-2026-44712 completes seven-CVE agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader pattern; Trail of Bits taxonomy lands
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday AutoGen CVE-2026-44612 (CVSS 8.9 checkpoint-deserialization RCE) plus Semantic Kernel CVE-2026-44638 (CVSS 8.4 plugin-manifest SSRF) landed Sunday-evening Pacific with same-day Microsoft patches (AutoGen v0.5.18, Semantic Kernel v1.36.0 plus out-of-band dotnet advisory); Trail of Bits cataloged both as following the May 8 CrewAI + Haystack pattern. Today LangChain CVE-2026-44712 (CVSS 8.7) lands Monday-morning Pacific — a LangGraph checkpoint-deserialization vulnerability matching the AutoGen pattern — with LangChain shipping LangGraph v0.7.2 same-day plus a backport advisory for v0.5.x and v0.6.x branches the NHS England blocklist references. Trail of Bits publishes a Monday extended write-up taxonomizing seven agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader CVEs across the May 5-11 wave (CrewAI, Haystack, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, LangChain, plus the Friday LangGraph CVE-2026-44012 and LiteLLM CVE-2026-44188), proposing a signed-checkpoint plus manifest-allowlist-validation common-mitigation pattern enforced at the framework boundary.

items.headline: Claude Code 3.0 day-four telemetry: 19,800 skills (+15.1 percent, first sub-20-percent day); Mythos cohort reaches 48 after Check Point/Leonardo/Saab sign
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday day-three lifted published skills to 17,200 (+24.6 percent), installs to 1.46M (a 64 percent acceleration), auto-quarantines to 29, with three sovereign-cloud tenants (BAE Systems UK, Rheinmetall AG Germany, Thales SA France) signing the Mythos rider on Sunday lifting the gated cohort to 44. Today day-four lifts published skills to 19,800 (+15.1 percent — first sub-20-percent daily gain since launch) with installs to 1.92M across the fourth 24 hours (a 32 percent acceleration). Auto-quarantines reach 36. Three additional enterprise customers sign the contractual ethics-and-misuse rider on the Monday business open: Israel's Check Point Software Technologies, Italy's Leonardo SpA, and Sweden's Saab AB — lifting the gated cohort to 48. Simon Willison's Monday note documents the per-tenant attestation-log audit-trail review now reproduces deterministically across 48 gated tenants via the open-source verification harness shipped Saturday, completing the Verifiable Per-Tenant Capability Attestation paper's lived demonstration cycle.

items.headline: Hyperscaler registry interop: AWS Bedrock OpenAI ChatGPT Enterprise interop pulls to GA two months early
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday AWS Bedrock Agent Registry's OpenAI ChatGPT Enterprise interop moved from private preview to public preview for FedRAMP-Moderate tenants ahead of the previously-communicated Q3 GA; Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Governance Center added parallel public-preview interop with the Claude Code 3.0 sandboxed-skill registry; Microsoft Azure AI Foundry Skill Catalog added South Korea PIPC + New Zealand GCSB cyber-eval reciprocity attestation fields. Today the AWS Bedrock + OpenAI ChatGPT Enterprise interop moves from public preview to general availability for FedRAMP-Moderate tenants Monday morning — two months ahead of the previously-communicated Q3 GA — citing Sunday public-preview workload telemetry as the launch-readiness signal. Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Governance Center adds a Monday changelog covering signed-skill provenance verification for the Mistral Workflows signed-export format shipped Sunday-night. Microsoft Azure AI Foundry Skill Catalog adds Israel National Cyber Directorate + Italy National Cybersecurity Agency cyber-eval reciprocity attestation fields, mirroring the new tenant signings on the Anthropic side.

items.headline: Mistral Workflows day-eleven lands UK HMRC as third sovereign-cloud central-government reference
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday day-ten landed Germany's Bundesagentur fuer Arbeit (Federal Employment Agency) for unemployment-claim anomaly-detection routing as the second central-government sovereign-cloud reference after France DGFiP, lifting paid Workflows tenancy to 304 customers and daily executions to 4.7M, with bidirectional Workflows-Codestral interop with OpenAI Codex CLI Plan-Apply export + Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 signed-export. Today day-eleven lands the United Kingdom's HM Revenue and Customs for value-added-tax fraud-detection routing as the third central-government sovereign-cloud reference, citing the same control-plane separation plus sovereign-cloud execution-worker model as the DGFiP and Bundesagentur references and citing the Sunday-shipped South Korea PIPC + New Zealand GCSB cyber-eval reciprocity attestation fields as the operative tenant-policy schema. Paid tenancy crosses 318 customers; daily executions reach 5.1M. The Workflows-Codestral bidirectional interop now adds Microsoft Azure AI Foundry Skill Catalog, completing the three-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix.

items.headline: Unsloth Monday: tensor-parallel router-attention on dual-Hopper, INT4 ONNX export, Qwen3-Next recipe; vLLM v0.11.2 ships parallel tensor-parallel disaggregated-prefill
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Unsloth's Sunday changelog added a multi-GPU NCCL backend for consumer dual-GPU workstation tiers, an ONNX export path removing the PEFT runtime dependency, and a Triton kernel trimming router-attention-step latency by 22 percent on Llama 4 Behemoth and Kimi K2.6, alongside a Hacker News Mixtral 8x22B router-only reproduction on dual RTX 5090 at 12 percent peak combined VRAM with 74 percent accuracy recovery. Today the Monday changelog adds a fourth refinement: a tensor-parallel mode for the router-attention forward pass on dual-Hopper workstation tiers (H100 SXM5 + H100 PCIe) reporting a further 17 percent peak combined VRAM reduction plus a 28 percent forward-pass latency improvement, an extended ONNX export path supporting INT4 quantization for Llama 4 + Codestral + Kimi K2.6, and a community Qwen3-Next 480B-A40B MoE recipe at 9 percent peak combined VRAM on quad-RTX 6000 Ada. In parallel vLLM v0.11.2 ships a Monday tensor-parallel disaggregated-prefill mode for dual-H100 SXM5 + PCIe workstations; Yotta Labs places the shared-prefix workload at 15,920 tok/s on vLLM vs 17,720 tok/s on SGLang RadixArk v0.5.5 — the throughput gap narrows to 11.3 percent (vs 16.7 percent Sunday). Cloudflare Infire reports the L40S edge-tier gap closes to a 1.25x Infire advantage (vs 1.40x Sunday).

items.headline: Tenstorrent Galaxy third-wave shipments land first Asia-Pacific neocloud commitments; AMD Helios passes 8.0GW
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Tenstorrent confirmed second-wave Sunday shipments adding 5 to CoreWeave (13 total), 4 to Lambda (10), 3 to Crusoe (7), 4 first-wave to Vultr, and 2 to Hyundai Metaplant (5), with the IPO bridge round at $3.4B fully closed (Bain Capital Ventures, Fidelity, Vy Capital, Atomico, Founders Fund); AMD Helios + MI450 commitment book passed 7.0GW after Tencent + Alibaba Sunday confirmations. Today third-wave shipments add 4 racks to CoreWeave (17 total), 3 to Lambda (13), 2 to Crusoe (9), 3 to Vultr (7), 2 to Hyundai Metaplant (7), plus first-wave Asia-Pacific neocloud commitments to Yotta Labs India (4), KT Cloud South Korea (3), and Sakura Internet Japan (2), reflecting Indo-Pacific reciprocity-cohort-aligned sovereign-cloud growth. Cumulative shipments cross 72 racks against the 280-rack first-half capacity target. AMD Helios + MI450 commitment book passes 8.0GW on Monday's confirmation of 0.6GW SoftBank Sakai plus 0.4GW NTT Data sovereign-cloud commitments.

items.headline: Cerebras CS-4 sample allocation slips to late-Q1 2027; Apple joins both Vera Rubin cohort and AMD MI450 commitment book
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday AIwire's Sunday three-vendor cross-vendor reconciliation set Cerebras CS-4 first-customer engineering samples at Q1 2027 with OpenAI as the lead-customer of record under the $10B multi-year supply agreement; Nvidia Vera Rubin sample-allocation spanned Microsoft Azure + Google Cloud + AWS + Oracle + OpenAI + Meta + CoreWeave + Lambda + Crusoe + Anthropic with H1 2027 NVL576 rack production volume; AMD Helios + MI450 commitment book passed 7.0GW. Today Cerebras's Monday Cerebras Engineering update slides OpenAI's lead-customer engineering-sample allocation to late-Q1 2027 (vs Q1 2027 floor in Sunday's reconciliation), reflecting the post-IPO investor-relations call's manufacturing-capacity expansion; Nvidia's Monday Vera Rubin update adds Apple to the cohort sharing H1 2027 NVL576 rack production volume; AMD's MI450 Monday hyperscaler-update note adds Apple at a 0.8GW initial allocation tied to Apple's on-prem AI-training estate expansion. The four-vendor capacity-addition shape reaches H2-2026-through-H1-2027 with an Apple-anchored extension.

items.headline: Atlas commercial roster Monday: Hyundai Metaplant LoRA fine-tune posts 4.1 percent cycle-time gain; Optimus Gen 3 doubles to 24 units active and demonstrates first multi-station hand-off
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Hyundai Robotics Metaplant Application Center provisioned its first per-task Atlas LoRA fine-tune on the Tenstorrent Galaxy rack using the Unsloth router-only LoRA recipe plus the new multi-GPU NCCL backend, with first results expected Tuesday; Dangjin posted a zero-MTBF clean-full-week milestone, Kia Zilina completed a second full shift on A-pillar subassembly, and LG Holland activated Sunday afternoon (24 hours ahead of plan) with 18 of 30 units on cell-stacking; the first 12 Optimus Gen 3 units completed a full 8-hour shift at a 1.2x human-baseline envelope. Today the first Atlas LoRA fine-tune for Dangjin rolling-mill pickup completes Sunday-evening Korea time with a 4.1 percent cycle-time improvement; policy distillation to the 60-unit Dangjin commercial roster is running with a Monday-evening Korea-time rollout target. Kia Zilina completes a third full shift cycle with zero MTBF-impacting incidents; LG Holland scales to 24 active units (vs 18 Sunday). A second cohort of 12 Optimus Gen 3 units activates at Fremont bringing total active count to 24 of the 240-unit allocation; cycle-time tightens to a 1.15x envelope; Tesla Robotics posts a 120-second clip showing eight units performing a coordinated three-station hand-off chain — the first multi-station coordination demonstration in production.

items.headline: Sovereign-cloud composition verification arxiv extends the multi-tenant attestation theorem chain to jurisdiction boundaries
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday two Sunday preprints landed: Multi-Tenant MCP Tool-Call Graph Verification with Formal Composition Rules (arxiv 2605.06012) extended the May 9 Verifiable Per-Tenant Capability Attestation paper with multi-tenant generalization (MIT CSAIL + ETH Zurich + Anthropic + Microsoft authorship), and Self-Generated Process Critique Decomposition for Math Reasoning (arxiv 2605.06034) reported 1.8-2.4 percent absolute gain when critiques are organized into chain-of-verification structure; DeepMind shipped a v3 ablation on the Unsloth multi-GPU NCCL backend. Today End-to-End Sovereign-Cloud Composition Verification for Agentic AI (arxiv 2605.06298) extends the Sunday multi-tenant theorem with a sovereign-cloud-jurisdiction composition framework providing formal verification of jurisdiction-boundary-crossing capability gating with the EU AI Act Section 51 + UK AISI + Singapore IMDA + Japan AISI + South Korea PIPC + New Zealand GCSB reciprocity-attestation field schemas as named verifiable constraints (MIT CSAIL + ETH Zurich + Anthropic + Microsoft + EU AI Office authorship). Stable Long-Context RL via Router-Aware Advantage Decomposition v4 adds a Monday extension closing the long-context training-stability gap on dual-H100 PCIe tensor-parallel router-attention plus pre-tested integration against vLLM v0.11.2.

items.headline: Signed-Checkpoint + Manifest-Allowlist joint preprint responds to Trail of Bits seven-CVE taxonomy with reference implementations and mid-June framework commitments
items.diff_narrative: Today opens a fresh story-thread absent yesterday: DeepMind + Meta AI + Anthropic co-publish a Monday joint preprint Signed-Checkpoint and Manifest-Allowlist Verification for Agentic AI Frameworks (arxiv 2605.06342) responding directly to the Trail of Bits Monday seven-CVE taxonomy by proposing a common signed-checkpoint format compatible across LangGraph, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, CrewAI, Haystack, and LiteLLM, plus a manifest-allowlist-validation schema enforced at the framework boundary; the paper provides reference implementations in Python and Rust plus formal compositional safety proofs covering the seven CVE pattern instances. Microsoft, LangChain, and the CrewAI maintainer team publish parallel Monday commitments to ship the signed-checkpoint format and manifest-allowlist-validation schema as a default in the next minor-version release of each respective framework, with a coordinated mid-June target window. This pre-empts the predicted Q4 2026 framework-default landing by closing the mitigation-pattern coordination cycle inside one news cycle.
